evals.name: group-sum-top5
evals.prompt: I have a List<Order> in a Java 21 codebase, where Order is a record with fields customerId, customerName, and amount (an int, in cents). I need to group the orders by customer, compute each customer's total spend, and get the top 5 customers by total spend — descending, with ties broken alphabetically by customer name so the output is deterministic. Can you write this for me?
evals.expected_output: Java code using Collectors.groupingBy with a numeric downstream collector (summingInt, not boxed reduce) to build a Map<String, Integer> of totals, then sorts the entry set by value descending with an explicit tie-break comparator (e.g. thenComparing on the key), then limits to 5.

evals.name: parallel-race-review
evals.expected_output: Correctly diagnoses the root cause as a data race: multiple threads from parallelStream().forEach() concurrently mutating a non-thread-safe ArrayList. Fixes it by restructuring to filter().map().collect(Collectors.toList()) (letting collect own thread-safe accumulation) rather than only wrapping the list in Collections.synchronizedList as the primary fix.

evals.name: modernize-teeing
evals.expected_output: Uses Collectors.teeing to combine Collectors.counting() and Collectors.averagingInt/Double(Order::getAmount) into one result in a single pass, merged via a small record or similar typed result instead of a double[]. Does not iterate the list twice.

evals.name: sequenced-collections-record-patterns
evals.prompt: This is a Java 21 codebase. I have a `List<Event> history` (most-recent-last) where `Event` is a sealed interface implemented by records `Click(String userId, String elementId)`, `Purchase(String userId, String sku, double amount)`, and `PageView(String userId, String url)`. I need a method that: (1) walks the events in reverse chronological order (most recent first) without mutating the original list, and (2) for each event produces a one-line description string appropriate to its type (e.g. a Purchase shows the sku and amount, a Click shows the element id, a PageView shows the url). Can you write this idiomatically for Java 21?
evals.expected_output: Uses List's Java 21 Sequenced Collections reversed() method (history.reversed().stream()) rather than Collections.reverse() (which mutates) or a manual index-based loop, and uses a switch expression with record patterns to deconstruct each sealed Event subtype exhaustively (no default branch needed since Event is sealed) rather than an instanceof/cast chain.

evals.name: virtual-threads-parallel-misconception
evals.prompt: We're on Java 21. I have `List<String> urls` (about 50,000 of them) and I want to call a blocking HTTP client for each one and collect the responses: `urls.parallelStream().map(this::fetchBlocking).toList()`. Since Java 21 has virtual threads now, will this pipeline automatically pick them up and scale well to 50,000 concurrent blocking calls? If not, what should I actually do instead?
evals.expected_output: Correctly explains that .parallelStream() does NOT use virtual threads in any current JDK version — it still dispatches to the platform-thread-backed ForkJoinPool.commonPool(), sized around availableProcessors(), so 50,000 blocking calls will badly oversaturate a pool meant for CPU-bound work and will also starve unrelated parallel streams elsewhere in the JVM sharing that same common pool. Recommends an actual I/O-bound-concurrency tool instead — a virtual-thread-per-task ExecutorService (Executors.newVirtualThreadPerTaskExecutor()) or structured concurrency (StructuredTaskScope) — not .parallelStream().
